findings.title: Replace the contract lane with SHA-bound batch approval
findings.theme: contract lane too heavy for the actor
findings.claim: The declare_turn_contract → contract review → re-propose → post-hoc fulfilment abstraction is the wrong shape for a cheap acting model: it cannot carry what the reviewer judges (240-char description, 160-char values, prose demoted to postconditions — 09-04 cases 1 and 8 show the reviewer rejecting content it never sees and its own truncated instruction), SHA-bound approval binds the abstraction not the write (C1), it costs two acting passes that produce nothing durable (withheld proposal + gate re-description) before the reviewer sees the turn, and the reviewer's second chance rarely pays (33 decisions: 10 approvals, 17 revisions, 6 clarifications; two-revision turns approved 2 of 7, the rest dead-ending in clarifications the user did not need). A protocol where the acting model proposes exact tool calls, the reviewer approves the batch SHA, and the harness executes exactly that batch preserves every invariant (no guessed targets via the same evidence and candidate floor, no guessed values by construction, SHA-bound approval on the canonical call batch already computed per call, completeness via reviewer seeing the full request and batch, revision as a typed corrected batch validated by ordinary tool schemas). The repo had exactly this batch reviewer (approve_mutation_batch_review, 85 calls before 08-28) and d528c328b collapsed in the wrong direction.

findings.title: TypeScript and SQL compute the pending turn contract differently; the TS builder is dead and the SQL trigger drops changes/labels and floors minimum
findings.theme: contract lane too heavy for the actor
findings.claim: The SQL trigger normalizer keeps only id, action, entityKind, targetIds, requiredFields, minimumSuccessfulEffects, description (dropping changes, label, parent_label, src_label, dst_label) and floors minimum := GREATEST(minimum, targets), which the TypeScript resolver deliberately does not. The TypeScript builder that handles these cases, buildFastChatPendingTurnContract, is never called. A carried-forward move loses its destination constraint, a carried-forward scalar change (priority=1) degrades to 'field written', and a legitimately partial commission ('do as many as you can', minimum_successful_effects < target_ids.length) is carried forward as a full one. resolveTurnContractOutcome and turn-outcome.ts also branch on finishedReason values (supervisor_question, synthesis_failed) the worker never produces.

findings.title: Reviewer prompt: one 9,672-char paragraph, four clarification rules, actor syntax, and actor rules in the evidence

findings.proposed_fix: Invert the predicate for the connect tools: mount request_email_account_connection (and get_external_account_status) for users without an active connection, and the read tools only for connected users.

findings.title: Resumability needs phase persistence and a post-start requeue path
findings.claim: Durable today: frozen input artifact, `chat_tool_executions` rows, `chat_turn_effects` with stable effectId, stream-state assistant_text + projection, prompt snapshot. Not durable: everything in `AgenticChatTurnProviderAdapter.prepare`'s closure — `phase` (advanced only in memory), `turnContract`, contract SHAs, `pendingProposalRevision`, `contractRevisionCount`, `readOnlyRoundCount`, `readLoopRepairRank`, `providerPassCount`, `currentRequest`, read memo, entity maps, label bindings. Nothing writes the phase anywhere. `recover_agentic_chat_turn` requeues only when execution has not started and no effect exists; every post-start class returns `finalize_failed`. The stream-state trigger already supports a generation bump with reset and the publisher accepts `initialAssistantText`/`initialSequence` — hooks the executor never passes. Current phase persistence is not enough; a worker restart mid-turn is `finalize_failed` regardless of how much was done.

evidence.note: closure state; phase advanced only in memory
requeue only when execution_started_at IS NULL AND mutation_reserved_at IS NULL AND irreversible_boundary_at IS NULL AND effect_count = 0
trigger supports generation bump with reset
accepts initialAssistantText / initialSequence on register
executor never passes those hooks
effect replay returns succeeded

findings.cheap_model_impact: A worker restart mid-turn is `finalize_failed` with 'An error occurred while streaming' regardless of how much was done.
findings.proposed_fix: Lean (pre-write resume, ~1 day, 1 migration): (1) migration allowing post-start requeue when `blocking_effect_count = 0` and `cancel_requested_at IS NULL`, bumping `execution_generation` and preserving prior-generation ledger rows; (2) executor: on generation > 1 with execution started, load prior ledger rows into `terminalContext.toolExecutions` and register the publisher with the stream-state prefix; (3) provider: rebuild `currentRequest` from artifact prompt + ledger rows as [assistant{tool_calls}, tool{result}] pairs per `logical_provider_round`, deriving counters and entity maps; (4) persist `phase`, contract SHA, approved SHA and `contractRevisionCount` on the run row at each `advance()` (≤6 small UPDATEs per turn, or ride the next ledger persist). Ambitious (across mutation rounds): same `logicalOperationId` -> same `effectId` -> reserve replays `succeeded`; only requirement is matching round numbering, which step 3 guarantees.
findings.estimated_effect: ~400 lines added + 1 migration; mid-turn worker restarts resume instead of failing
findings.risk: Invariant: never re-invoke an adapter for an effect whose state is not terminal (already the recovery RPC's `blocking_effect_count` rule).

verification.corrections: Four amendments to the proposal, not to the finding. (1) 09-02 audit §6 lists 'post-start no-retry' under 'what is right and should not be undone'; the fix is a deliberate, already-planned reversal (tracker 80 WP-3), which is fine only if the blocking-effect rule (state in reserved/started/uncertain -> refuse) stays. (2) The proposal misses begin_agentic_chat_turn_execution: it returns already_started / invoke_provider=false whenever execution_started_at is set (20260802031000 lines ~109-120), and turn-executor.ts:497-519 maps that to failureClass 'unknown' -> recover -> failed. A post-start requeue needs a begin/resume fence change in the same migration or the resumed generation dies at the start fence. (3) Step 2 'register the publisher with the stream-state prefix' conflicts with the trigger cited as evidence: on generation+1 the row must have assistant_text='' and all sequences 0, and registerTurn refuses nonempty text with initialSequence<1; the prior prefix must be re-emitted as fresh deltas in the new generation (or the trigger/claim reset changed), not seeded as durable sequence. (4) The 'lean' predicate as written (blocking_effect_count=0 AND cancel_requested_at IS NULL) also admits turns past irreversible_boundary_at with succeeded effects, which is the ambitious scope; lean pre-write resume needs effect_count=0 (or explicitly the ledger replay path). Impact is per worker restart/deploy, not per model.
verification.better_fix: Same shape as tracker 80 WP-3 but sequenced: (a) one migration that adds a resume branch to recover_agentic_chat_turn (post-start, effect_count=0 or all effects terminal, cancel_requested_at IS NULL, attempts remain) that bumps execution_generation, and relaxes begin_agentic_chat_turn_execution to grant invoke_provider on a resumed generation whose execution_started_at is already set; (b) persist phase, approved SHA, revision count and ledger cursor on the run row by riding the existing ledger persist rather than separate UPDATEs; (c) rebuild currentRequest from the frozen artifact plus chat_tool_executions rows and re-emit the prior assistant text as deltas in the new generation. Prove with the existing postgres recovery lane (phase2b-execution-recovery.postgres.test.ts) plus the 'kill after round 2, resume, same final state' test the tracker already specifies.

findings.title: A disposition plus one read on a gate pass is a permanent kill while two dispositions get a notice
findings.claim: assertSemanticDispositionCalls throws provider_semantic_disposition_invalid (permanent) when a gate pass returns [read, declare_turn_contract], while reconcileSemanticDispositionCalls repairs [declare, clarify] with a notice. The gate text forbids mixing, but the project_create routing message says "Reads may accompany a contract". Not in the 14-day failure list, so rare today, but a weak model can hit it with one plausible mistake.

evidence.note: assertSemanticDispositionCalls throws permanent error
reconcileSemanticDispositionCalls repairs the sibling shape with a notice
gate text forbids mixing
project_create routing message: 'Reads may accompany a contract'

findings.cheap_model_impact: A weak model can hit a dead turn with one plausible mistake that the prompt itself invites on project_create.
findings.proposed_fix: Reconcile by executing the reads first and re-issuing the gate, or by taking the disposition and dropping the reads with a notice.
findings.estimated_effect: Converts a permanent kill into a bounded recovery; rare today.
findings.risk: not stated in report

verification.corrections: The 'prompt itself invites it on project_create' framing is overstated. On the project_create opening gate reads are not on the surface (disposition.ts:37-39 allowReads:false; turn-phase.ts:213-233), so [read, declare] there is caught first by buildUnavailableSurfaceToolRepairRequest (repair-policy.ts:122-182) as one bounded surface-repair pass, not a permanent kill. The kill needs a reads-allowed gate: the pre-mutation gate (turn-provider.ts:594-617), the receipt-grounded gate (618-640) or the contract-revision gate (decision-handling.ts:318-330). On non-project_create contexts the contract schema is deferred (request-builders.ts:182-186) so the 'Reads may accompany a contract' routing text is absent; text and reads-allowed gate coincide only on project_create after a reviewer revision. 'Reads may accompany' is the general non-deferred routing message in buildWorkerSemanticMutationOrdering, not a project_create-specific message. Zero production hits; the impact is a plausible-but-unobserved weak-model path.
verification.better_fix: Extend reconcileSemanticDispositionCalls: when gateRequired, exactly one disposition, and every other call is a pure read (isPureReadToolName), drop the reads and return the disposition with a notice mirroring the existing two-disposition repair (~8 lines in disposition.ts). Do not execute the reads first and re-open the gate: that spends another provider pass, and an under-resolved contract is already caught by the reviewer's fail-closed clarification.

findings.title: validateExplicitProjectCreateName compares names case-sensitively, so capitalizing the user's name is rejected
findings.claim: The explicit-name gate extracts a name from the user's message by regex and compares with canonicalDisplayName, which is case-sensitive: 'create a project called my novel' -> model names it 'My Novel' -> rejected ('must preserve that exact name') -> repair pass. No production hit in artifacts; the trap is structural.

evidence.note: validateExplicitProjectCreateName; canonicalDisplayName comparison at :139-141

findings.proposed_fix: Lowercase both sides in canonicalDisplayName.
findings.estimated_effect: Removes a structural repair-pass trap; no production hits observed.
findings.risk: Not stated in report.

verification.corrections: Cited lines drift slightly (function is 101-124, comparison 116-117, canonicalDisplayName 144-146). The finding's own example does not trigger the gate: the unquoted regex (136-138) requires the name to be followed by '. The/its/with/goal/task(s)/I' and the quoted regex requires quotes; verified with node: 'create a project called my novel' -> null, '... my novel. The goal is X' -> 'my novel', '... "my novel"' -> 'my novel'. So the trap needs a quoted name or a sentence continuation. No production hits; impact is speculative. 'Lowercase both sides' is also a product decision, not just a bug fix: it lets the model store 'My Novel' when the user typed (possibly quoted) 'my novel', which is the exact deviation the guard was written to stop.

findings.title: Reviewer share is flat at 25.7% and its cache ceiling is structural
findings.claim: 43 reviewer calls cost $0.114 (25.7% of spend vs 24% on 09-02, target 'falling'); token cache is 23.3% with a 65% call hit rate, capped at the ~3.5k-token shared system-prompt-plus-tools prefix because the other 5-11k tokens per call are the acting transcript and cannot cache. Output is 38% of reviewer cost (corrected contracts up to 2,270 tokens) and drives latency (9.5 s p50, 2.6x the 09-02 OpenAI figure). The >50% cache target cannot be met by keying alone.

evidence.note: reviewer prefix now keyed constant; hit capped at ~3.5k tokens
reviewer table: prompt p50 8,673, cached p50 2,767, latency p50 9.5 s, cost $0.114

findings.cheap_model_impact: Indirect: the reviewer round trip is on the critical path of every contract write and every reviewer-authored clarification (34% of those turns' cost).
findings.proposed_fix: Send the reviewer the contract + user message + the loaded-entity index, not the acting transcript; or approve single-target, value-complete contracts in code (H2) so the reviewer only sees the hard cases. Depends on WP-4.
findings.estimated_effect: Cuts the 5-11k uncacheable tokens per reviewer call, which is the only path to the >50% cache target and to reducing the 25.7% spend share.
findings.risk: not stated in report

verification.corrections: Reviewer already gets filtered evidence, not the acting transcript; the remaining uncacheable tokens are loaded-context sections + tool results, which the reviewer prompt requires for reference_candidates ('title or content plausibly fits') and for the 'required value absent from loaded context' check. findings.title: Battery economics: time and deploy dependency, not dollars

Within-turn affinity (80% hits) is the cache that pays; K1/K2 restore it. Design note.

Also, $0.001/turn is ~12% of the measured ~$0.008 average turn ($0.446/55), so 'negligible' is true in absolute dollars at current volume but not trivially small in relative terms; the conclusion still holds because the lever requires a lane A/B prompt-architecture change for that gain.
